policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'on the back' directly reflects ὄπισθεν; ἔξωθεν would express the outside rather than the back.
ASV 'Who is worthy' supplies the copula naturally for either the base verbless clause or the reading with explicit ἐστιν.
ASV has simply 'in the heaven' and no 'above,' excluding the addition ἄνω.
ASV's repeated 'or' can render either οὐδέ ... οὐδέ or οὔτε ... οὔτε in this negative series.
ASV 'I wept' is required by the first-person verb whether or not the explicit pronoun ἐγώ is present.
ASV 'hath overcome to open the book' directly reflects the infinitive ἀνοῖξαι rather than the participial alternative.
The readings are orthographic/accentual forms of the same perfect participle and both yield ASV 'standing.'
ASV participial 'having' does not expose the grammatical gender difference between ἔχων and ἔχον.
English relative 'which' does not distinguish masculine οἵ from neuter ἃ.
ASV bare participial 'sent forth' does not securely distinguish perfect ἀπεσταλμένοι from present ἀποστελλόμενα.
ASV 'which are the prayers' may use a definite predicate either with or without the Greek article before προσευχαί.
ASV says Christ purchased 'men' unto God and has no object 'us,' excluding the addition ἡμᾶς.
ASV 'a kingdom' directly reflects βασιλείαν rather than plural personal 'kings.'
ASV present 'they reign' directly reflects βασιλεύουσιν rather than future βασιλεύσουσιν.
ASV heard 'a voice' directly, not 'as a voice,' excluding the addition ὡς.
ASV's single initial article scopes the coordinated list and does not distinguish an additional Greek article before the final 'blessing.'
ASV's one finite 'is' at the start of the relative clause can govern the entire locative series whether or not ἐστίν is repeated after 'sea.'
ASV's explicit neuter 'all things' supports πάντα rather than masculine πάντας.
ASV 'sitteth on the throne' directly reflects dative τῷ θρόνῳ rather than genitive τοῦ θρόνου.
ASV ends verse 13 with 'for ever and ever' and has no Amen there, excluding the addition Ἀμήν.
ASV finite plural 'the four living creatures said Amen' directly reflects ἔλεγον rather than participial λέγοντα τὸ.
